questions.prompt: Acid-fast stain: what do the pink/red cells represent?
questions.explanation: Acid-fast cells keep the carbolfuchsin (pink/red); non-acid-fast cells are decolorized and counterstained blue.

why.A: Non-acid-fast cells take up methylene blue (blue).
why.B: This is an acid-fast stain, not a Gram stain.
why.D: Endospores stain green in the endospore stain.

questions.prompt: In this acid-fast stain, what color are the NON-acid-fast cells, and why?

options.text: Blue — they lose carbolfuchsin and take up methylene blue
Green — they take up malachite green

questions.explanation: Non-acid-fast cells are decolorized by acid-alcohol and counterstained with methylene blue.

why.B: Crystal violet isn't used in the acid-fast stain.
why.D: Malachite green is the endospore stain.

questions.prompt: What makes acid-fast bacteria resistant to most stains?

options.text: Waxy mycolic acids in the cell wall
A thick outer membrane with LPS

questions.explanation: Mycolic acid is very waxy: it resists phagocytosis, repels some antibiotics and repels most stains.

why.B: LPS is in the Gram-negative outer membrane.
why.C: Endospores are a separate survival structure.
why.D: Teichoic acids are a Gram-positive feature.

questions.prompt: What is the acid-fast stain used for clinically?

options.text: A quick preliminary test for tuberculosis and leprosy (Mycobacterium)
Choosing between Gram+ and Gram− antibiotics

questions.explanation: Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast stain: a preliminary, quick diagnostic for M. tuberculosis and M. leprae.

questions.prompt: What are the acid-fast stain reagents, in order?
questions.explanation: Acid-fast: carbolfuchsin (primary) → heat 5 min (mordant) → acid-alcohol 4 s (decolorizer) → methylene blue 30 s (counterstain).

why.D: The acid-fast mordant is heat, and the counterstain is methylene blue.

questions.prompt: In both the acid-fast and endospore stains, what serves as the mordant?
questions.explanation: The slide sits over a weigh boat on the hot plate for 5 minutes under stain-soaked paper towel.

why.A: Iodine is the Gram stain mordant.

questions.prompt: During heating, why must you keep reapplying the primary stain to the paper towel?

options.text: To make the stain hot enough to boil
The paper must not be allowed to dry
To rinse excess dye into the weigh boat

questions.explanation: Don't let the paper dry — reapply the primary stain as needed, and don't drip stain onto the hot plate.

why.A: The goal is to keep the paper wet.
why.D: The weigh boat simply catches drips.

questions.prompt: How long is acid-alcohol applied in the acid-fast stain?
questions.explanation: Acid-alcohol for 4 seconds — be careful to avoid excess decolorization.

why.A: 10 seconds is the Gram stain alcohol step.
why.B: 30 seconds is the methylene blue counterstain.

questions.prompt: Endospore stain: what color are the endospores and the vegetative cells?
questions.explanation: Endospores keep malachite green; vegetative cells are decolorized by water and counterstained pink with safranin.

why.A: Reversed: malachite green stays in the spores.

questions.prompt: What are the endospore stain reagents, in order?

options.text: Malachite green → iodine → alcohol → methylene blue

questions.explanation: Schaeffer-Fulton endospore stain: malachite green → heat 5 min → water 5 s → safranin 30 s.

why.D: The endospore mordant is heat, the decolorizer water, the counterstain safranin.

questions.prompt: What is the decolorizer in the endospore stain?
questions.explanation: Water for 5 seconds decolorizes vegetative cells; endospores keep the malachite green.

questions.prompt: What is the endospore stain used for?
questions.explanation: The endospore stain detects endospore-forming members of Bacillus and Clostridium.

questions.prompt: This micrograph shows a single bacterial cell with a dense internal structure. What is that structure?
questions.explanation: Endospores are produced in response to stress and resist desiccation, UV, extreme heat, freezing, disinfectants and even antibiotics.

why.B: A capsule is outside the cell wall.

questions.prompt: Why does slide E (endospore stain) use a single species smear instead of a mixed one?

options.text: Mixed smears can't be heat fixed on the hot plate
Only one organism (Organism 4) is checked for spores
Malachite green kills any second species present
The acid-alcohol step requires a single species

questions.explanation: G and A are mixed smears (to compare cell types); E is a single species smear of Organism 4.

why.A: All three smears are heat fixed.
why.C: The protocol simply uses one organism.

questions.prompt: Which statement about endospores is FALSE?

options.text: They resist desiccation, UV and extreme heat
They act like a 'stasis chamber' preserving genetic information
Spores in a 250-million-year-old salt crystal were revived
Bacillus, Clostridium and Clostridioides form them
They are produced when nutrients are plentiful

questions.explanation: Endospores are produced in response to stressful environmental conditions, such as a lack of nutrients.
